Hi Jonas,

We observed a spike in errors and sustained latency on our Redwood inference endpoints yesterday (2026-03-28) between ~17:05 and ~17:28 UTC that impacted a subset of production traffic. Customers reported 502s and timeouts; our telemetry shows p95/p99 latency increases and about ~3.6% failed requests for the period.

Per our contract (SLA section), we believe this may qualify for an SLA credit and we also need a postmortem for our compliance records. Can you confirm: 1) whether Redwood has recorded an incident for this window, 2) whether this counts toward SLA eligibility, and 3) the expected timeline for a formal postmortem and any documentation you can share?

I've attached our SLO export for the day (slo-summary.csv) to help correlate events. Please loop in anyone on your side who needs to own the incident details — this is time-sensitive for our renewal discussion.

Thanks,
Elena Martin

Subject: Re: Possible SLA breach on 2026-03-28 — Incident INC-20260328-17 details and postmortem plan

Hi all,

Sharing the technical summary for INC-20260328-17 and the plan for a postmortem. Apologies for the delay — investigations required correlating control-plane and network telemetry.

Summary (high level):
- Incident ID: INC-20260328-17
- Window: 2026-03-28 17:05:12 UTC -> 2026-03-28 17:28:37 UTC (23 minutes, 25 seconds)
- Impact: Intermittent 502/504 responses and elevated p99 latency for inference endpoints in eu-west-1. Aggregate failed-request rate ~3.6% for Streamline AI traffic; p99 increased from ~420ms baseline to ~3.2s during peak.
- Root cause (initial): Network interface flaps on a subset of routing gear in eu-west-1 caused transient request misrouting and backend timeouts. This cascaded into queueing on the serving nodes and increased tail latency for affected shards.
- Mitigation steps taken: rerouted traffic off impacted network paths at 17:08 UTC, scaled serving pool and cleared KV cache hot-rows by 17:22 UTC, full recovery by 17:28:37 UTC.

Evidence and artifacts:
- Incident timeline (detailed): https://app.redwood.com/incidents/INC-20260328-17
- Request traces: https://traces.redwood.com/trace/INC-20260328-17 (access available to Streamline SRE team)
- Attached: request_postmortem_template.docx (we'll populate with detailed timeline, RCA, and action items)

SLA credit eligibility note: per our standard SLA calculation, credits are based on total downtime impacting availability SLOs for dedicated endpoints. Based on the measured window and the impact you described, this incident appears to meet the threshold for a partial credit. We will run the formal calculation once we've reconciled request-level logs with your provided SLO export. Expect a credit calculation summary from finance within 5 business days after the postmortem is finalized.

Next steps we propose:
1) Joint postmortem session: Thu 2026-04-01 09:30 UTC (30m) — Jonas to coordinate invites.
2) Redacted postmortem draft: we'll circulate within 48 hours of the debrief with timeline, root cause, corrective actions, and target dates.
3) Credit calculation: finance will issue a calculation and proposed credit within 5 business days after the final postmortem.

If you need the credit expedited for your renewal timeline, please share the billing contact and any internal SLA clause you prefer we apply and we'll prioritize the calculation.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
SRE Lead — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
